title: Sleep schedule alarm settings need improvements (iPhone)
body:
If you need to skip a sleep schedule alarm 1x, you should be able to easily do this — this is a basic need that millions of users would have to do regularly since, say, their Monday morning alarm is no longer needed due to a long weekend. There should just be a “skip” button when you go to the sleep schedule menu. There’s not. The only way I’ve been able to do this is if I wait til past my bedtime, when I’m already supposed to be asleep, and the SLEEP focus setting turns on, and there may be a button to skip next days alarm or turn it off. 

If you’re on vacation it would also be great to be able to press a button putting your sleep schedule of alarms off for like a week and have them automatically turn back on on a scheduled date. So you don’t face the possibility of going back to work and not having an alarm on your first day back. 

On that note, I did have to manually turn off my sleep schedule alarms while on vacation, set a reminder to turn them back on when I was back before I started work, and manually turned them back on. However after doing so, my sleep schedule alarm did NOT go off the next morning and I missed my wake up and was late to work. A glitch to look into but also another reason to implement the improvement I suggested in the preceding/2nd paragraph :)

title: Feature Request
body:
Subject: Feature Request: Native Bowel Movement and Digestive Tracking in Apple Health
Dear Apple Health Development Team, Please consider adding a native "Bowel Movements" or comprehensive “Digestive” tracking category to the Apple Health app. While users can track basic symptoms like diarrhea or constipation, there is currently no way to log standard daily stool data, such as consistency using the Bristol Stool Scale. This feature is critical for millions of users who need to monitor medication side effects affecting gut motility, manage chronic conditions like IBS, or correlate digestive health with their food and fiber tracking. Integrating this into Apple Health would centralize vital gastrointestinal data alongside existing fitness and clinical records. Thank you for your time and continuous health innovations.

title: A UX overhaul
body:
Apple Health is already a highly proactive digital health platform, but I believe it has an opportunity to evolve further through product innovation and a more patient-centric design strategy. While the State of Mind feature offers an intuitive way to capture emotions using standardized mood selections, its note section is too limited to fully support users who need to document the circumstances surrounding their emotional state. From a user experience (UX) and customer value proposition perspective, expanding this capability would significantly enhance the feature’s utility.

The State of Mind feature could become a more comprehensive mental health tool by allowing users to record detailed observations about emotional triggers, symptoms, medication adherence, sleep quality, coping strategies, and significant life events immediately after they occur. This would create a richer repository of patient-generated health data (PGHD) that could be securely shared with healthcare providers whenever appropriate.

From a customer relationship management (CRM) perspective, enabling users to generate and share comprehensive mental health summaries before an appointment would improve communication between patients and clinicians, increase appointment efficiency, and support more informed clinical decision-making. If a patient misses an appointment or struggles to explain what they experienced over several weeks, these detailed entries could provide valuable context that might otherwise be forgotten.

This enhancement would also increase customer engagement, strengthen customer satisfaction, and improve long-term platform adoption by providing greater value to individuals managing psychological or behavioral health conditions. By continuously refining features that address real-world healthcare needs, Apple can reinforce its brand positioning as a leader in digital health innovation while building stronger customer loyalty.

Ultimately, expanding the State of Mind feature represents an opportunity for Apple to leverage continuous product development, market differentiation, and customer-centric innovation. By transforming a simple mood tracker into a comprehensive mental health documentation tool, Apple could strengthen its competitive advantage while delivering meaningful value to both patients and healthcare professionals.

title: HOPING TO GET MORE OPTIONS…
body: The Cycle Tracking part of the app could use a few tweaks. First, while the list of symptoms is decent, the list is incomplete, and there’s no option to elaborate on ones already there, like “Sleep Changes.” This one could be separated into sleeping more than usual, trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, and even didn’t sleep at all. There’s also a difference between a headache and a migraine, so both should be included. “Mood Changes” is ridiculously generic, too, and needs to be further broken down. Symptoms can also help to track an individual’s specific menstruation cycle and even help predict upcoming potential PMS! Also, there’s nothing to help individuals with perimenopausal cycles. I noticed my own pattern of skipping cycles every so many months, but the app did not. Not everyone understands how it all works, so including information (like the specifics on what “Spotting” really is that was already included a while ago), only for users in perimenopause and wondering if they might be in full menopause yet would be extremely useful. Those who reach menopause early, or are just curious about what to expect might even find it helpful—including the fact that plenty of women can still experience phantom, menstrual cycle symptoms even after reaching menopause. Please, update this portion of the app to include more symptoms, a place to make personal notes, and to predict cycles that are becoming irregular periodically due to natural aging.

author: Linda W.Carey

title: Worst period tracking ever
body:
When I saw how much Apple praised their period tracker this year I thought for sure they’ve added to it in the two years I went without an Apple phone. Nope! Still a horrible tracker that doesn’t let you record any DETAILS. Heavy spotting or light? Nope, just “spotting”. Cramps? Okay you can record that but you can’t record WHERE the cramps are or how intense they are. Are they throbbing or stabbing? This app doesn’t care, it maintains that all cramps (or any symptom) is created equally. Do you have irregular periods? This app will berate you with notifications. “It’s too early for your period, are you sure you have it?” Or if your period is late “you haven’t gotten your period yet, should I record it now?

This app was clearly engineered by a bunch of men who have no idea how periods work or what women need/want to track out every symptom. This app was created for the non average female who has a perfect period tied up with a little pink bow every month. 

And speaking of pink? Why is that color associated with our periods? Pink is a fun, girly, happy color, it’s not the color I would choose for lying in bed curled up in a ball for three days like the Grimm Reaper is waiting to take me away. 

Plus, for fitness, they STILL don’t have an option to add an injury. I’m sick of being told to push myself when I have a knee that can’t be pushed. 

Oh, and how is it possible that I only burned 36 calories on a two mile bike ride when my heart is pounding and my legs are going to fall off?

And if the Apple Watch 11 has a temperature sensor, why isn’t that tied in to the period tracking to help track ovulation? 

After 11 years, Apple is still failing at women’s health.

title: Almost there
body:
The app could be very useful for keeping track of my health but I find it frustrating that it isn’t comprehensive enough to be my only health app. 

My wishlist for updates to the app:

1. I can’t retroactively edit my medication records. I’m forgetful and would appreciate a way to easily keep track of what I’m taking — not just current but dates historically so I can see that I’m taking something I tried last year. A notes section would be great too to track side effects present. 

2. I can’t add custom symptoms to the symptom tracker. Even just having one single “other” would be helpful. In my case I would like to track my ADHD symptoms to see if there’s a pattern — I also have been getting tremors and seeing if there’s a pattern ( they show up X hours after taking medication or eating etc.) would be helpful. Disappointing that the app can’t include a little flexibility/customization beyond just what Apple is interested in. 

TL;DR — add more archival features and customization.

title: Apple Health App / Omron Connect Problems
body:
Sometime Mid-January 2026, the Omron Connect app (which we use only for blood pressure device syncing), started reporting bogus values to the Apple Health app, specifically:

* Body weight of -2.2 lbs
* BMI (body mass index) of 0

even though the blood pressure monitors paired with the app cannot report those measurements.

I am unsure why the Apple Health App had the Omron Connect app listed as a data source for Weight and BMI, but it is possible I turned that on casually when I first set up my BP monitor (i.e. selected “All Data” to be sent to HealthKit.

Apple HealthKit apparently compounds Omron’s bad app programming by doing NO data validation on the values written to it, neither excluding impossible values like a negative weight or zero BMI, but also not comparing the written value to see if it is within some medically reasonable distance of existing history (e.g. you can’t lose 50 pounds in one day). They should either (a) discard bogus data points, or (b) log them but flag them as not to be included in averages and trends.

The solution for me involved two steps:

* Turning off the Omron Connect app as a data source for anything other than blood pressure and pulse rate.
* Manually deleting all the bogus data points in the Apple Health App

author: Bob Hendricks

title: 🎈🐟cycle tracking math is incorrect🌶️💧
body:
cycle tracking must count from the first day of bleeding (day 1).

this app appears to reference a later flow date (end of bleeding or most recent entry), which shifts the cycle forward and creates incorrect predictions.

example from my data:
	•	period started feb 23 → this is day 1
	•	march 18 = cycle day 24

however, the app highlights a later “menstrual flow” date (~feb 27), which creates a ~4 day offset.

that means:
	•	correct: day 24
	•	app-influenced reference: ~day 20

this is not a small difference.
a 3–5 day shift directly affects ovulation and fertile window timing.

if predictions are based on that shifted reference instead of true day 1, they are biologically inaccurate.

this is not about cycle length or user error — it is a calculation anchor issue.

fix needed:
	•	always anchor to the first day of bleeding
	•	do not use last day of flow or most recent bleed entry
	•	allow users to verify or override the reference point

this has been consistent over time.

if this is functioning as designed, the design does not align with standard cycle tracking methods.

title: It works quietly
body:
Apple Health has quietly become one of the most important apps on my phone. It does not try to overwhelm you with noise. Instead, it collects your health data in one place and presents it clearly and calmly.

I use it daily to track heart data, activity, sleep, and trends over time. What I appreciate most is how everything connects. Workouts, heart rate, ECG recordings, steps, and even third-party apps all feed into one clean dashboard. It makes long-term patterns easy to spot without needing to dig through menus.

The privacy design is also reassuring. You stay in control of what data is shared and with which apps. That balance between powerful tracking and user control is rare.

It is not flashy, and that is exactly why it works. It feels stable, reliable, and thoughtfully designed. Over time, it quietly helps you become more aware of your habits and your health.

title: trend lines, not bar charts pls. Also overlays.
body:
I’ve been using Apple Health heavily since it first appeared. I link all kinds of apps to it. I’d love it to be my central tool, but it lacks two key features for actually being able to visualize your overall health picture: 

1) When you try to view your trend over time in “see more data”, it presents the data in a bar chart format, with a y-axis scale that makes it impossible to see your trend. It should have a fitted trend line on every graph so you can actually see ups and downs. A customizable axis scale would also help this immensely.

2) People who track their health stats, and are trying to improve them, or just want to see the effects of their lifestyle and lifestyle changes, want to see how each factor affects the others. The ability to overlay one health factor over another (and multiple factors) would be immensely powerful and motivating. How does my sleep affect my blood pressure? Is my exercise routine affecting my weight, and blood pressure? How does sleep affect my VO2? Without it, we are eyeballing, and flipping back and forth between each.

title: Dangerous medication tracking
body:

Users also get text messages to enter their medication’s taken into a log file. 
This double notification from both the reminders and the log can confuse people medications twice, what’s possibly fatal results.
I would prefer that if I get a reminder to take a medication and I enter that I have taken it, but that same information be entered into the log. Or if I enter the information into the log file that I have taken it, it should not show up in reminder to take it again. 
This app is very dangerous potentially.

title: I have a suggestion
body:
I like this app, but I have a suggestion. I use it mostly to track my steps; I really like to see how my step count changes over time, over months and years. 

I wish there was a way to customize the scale of the y-axis when it is showing you the bar graphs of your step count over a month-long period. 

As it is currently, the scale on the y-axis automatically changes to auto-fit for your highest day of the month. The problem is that this value can change dramatically for me from month-to-month, and it makes it difficult to get an intuitive sense of how my step count is changing over time as I am swiping through several months at a time. This also happens on the yearly scale, and I have a similar issue. 

I wish there was a way to fix the scale on the y-axis for when you want to swipe through several months or years of data, to see the ebb and flow of the step count more fluidly and intuitively without the y-axis scale changing constantly.

title: It’s okay but could be better
body:
The app is overall okay and I do really like being able to discretely enter medication usage on my watch instead of pulling out my phone, especially at work. 

The heart and blood oxygen trackers are convenient so I don’t need my conspicuous fingertip pulse oximeter as often. 
The medication tracking is the feature I use most, but it’s missing some important features. 

Having medications in the list to enter is nice, but rescue inhaler use isn’t automatically counted in the respiratory health section and needs to be manually entered and time stamped. No option for nebulizer usage either. When using an inhaler more than once a day the inconvenience is considerable and detracts from my user  experience. It would be greatly improved by allowing users to set an as-needed medication to automatically copy to the inhaler usage records. 

The medication options also don’t have an option for higher dosages on some medications, like Botox maxing out at 100 units when the actual max for medical usage can be over 300. I can attach a note with the real dosage but it’s unideal, when I want to share my real medication list I have to have a separate copy somewhere else with the correct information on it. 

In the profile options you can only set medications that influence heart rate as being calcium channel blockers or beta blockers. It leaves out stimulants and corticosteroids. No option available to manually enter non-template medications to fix that either. 

Entering medications taken late, like a night dose taken the morning after. That’s inaccurate and clunky given that I have to set the time to as being the on the intended day to register it as taken at all. So a dose intended for 10:00 pm Friday night needs to be entered as being taken on Friday evening if I took it at 2: 00am on Saturday. I compromise by entering as 2:00am on Friday but the inaccuracies make it really annoying to flip between days to list all medications actually consumed on Saturday.

The gait unevenness and step counting is nice but feels incomplete and doesn’t cover as much as I hoped. I would like an option to account for walking aids like my forearm crutch or comparison with when I take certain medications, so I can see compare how much they help with my limp

There needs to be sections on inputting data on your own and having the ability to take notes. Some days and months are going to be different than others. title: Too Buggy - Apple must fix it
body:
This review is for the medication portion of the app (particularly the Traditional Chinese version).

1. Sometimes med doesn’t record as logged after entering it manually by clicking “Taken” and “Done.”

2. The iPhone and iPad data don’t sync, or they take a long time to sync, causing confusion.

3. Sharing doesn’t give proper alerts to those receiving them, for info such as high fall risk.

4. The circles for all meds taken for the day don’t always show correctly; sometimes missing.

5. The UI is unintuitive. 

This app is revolutionary, has a lot of potential, and can be life-changing if it works as it should. The bugs make it hard to love, and may even be dangerous if we completely rely on it.

I have used both the U.S. and the Traditional Chinese versions. While the Traditional Chinese version is buggier, the U.S. version is also very buggy.

This cannot be the best Apple can do. Please fix it, Apple.

title: Cycle tracker
body:
I like this app for my medical tracking, period tracking,activity tracking, and others. I have participated in long term research projects around women’s health that I would otherwise been able to do.

Note to developers- While I love the period tracking, this is not just about how to get pregnant. It would be really useful to have a factor of “perimenopausal” to be able to better accurately account for all of the wild changes our bodies go through (these changes make us feel crazy because they are not tracked and studied!). This would be a great tool to studies the end of women’s reproductive health. How perimenopause affects  sleep, blood pressure, state of mind (which I don’t use regularly) etc and using AI to help predict better. One other thought is if perimenopause is a factor the cycle length options would automatically adjust (I just had a 21 day period, and now 45 days into this period and I think finally skipped one, but the app still says that my next period is due based on the cycle input. It never adjusts to say missed period, etc). I would think with the amount of data you have access to it could really help influence and inform the much needed studies into this time of every woman’s body.

title: Feature Request: Pill Inventory Tracking & Refill Reminders in Apple Health Medications
body:
Hi Apple Team,

I appreciate the Medications feature in Apple Health as it’s been invaluable for reminders, logging doses, and tracking adherence. However, I (and many others) would greatly benefit from the ability to track pill inventory and receive automatic refill reminders when my supply is running low.

Currently, there’s no way to enter the quantity on hand, subtract pills as I log doses, or get a heads-up when it’s time to request a refill. This is especially important for people managing multiple prescriptions, or splitting medication between different containers (like a main bottle and an on-the-go pill holder).

Please consider adding:
	•	Pill quantity tracking per medication
	•	Automatic deduction when doses are logged
	•	Refill reminder alerts based on remaining supply and schedule
	•	Ability to track pills in multiple locations (main bottle + pill organizer, etc.)

This would make Apple Health a truly complete tool for medication management and help prevent missed doses due to running out unexpectedly.

Thanks for considering!

title: Needs Major Enhancements
body:
The Health app has potential, but it needs serious improvement. Right now, most of the tracking is focused on 12-month increments, which isn’t very useful for people trying to monitor short-term progress. Users should be able to view trends over the past week, month, or three months to stay motivated and make real-time adjustments.

The app should also allow users to input height and weight and track changes over time. On top of that, it’s missing a basic calorie counter. Users should be able to log meals, track daily calorie intake, and set personal goals for calorie limits and weight loss. Some of the data currently shown feels irrelevant or lacks context. Adding more practical and customizable features would make this app far more helpful and user-friendly.

The scrolling date/time picker when manually entering a workout is a mess. First, if you enter an incorrect time, the app should prevent you from saving, NOT reset the start date, change PM to AM etc. Second, deleting a workout is way more work than it should be. I also ran into a bug where I accidentally clicked “Delete All”. Clicking “Cancel” just deleted all anyway.

I don’t know who coded this app, but they should be reassigned to something else.

title: Honest Review - Apple Health is a Complete Failure
body:
Absolutely useless. The Apple Health app is one of the most disappointing and frustrating experiences I’ve had with any app, especially one that’s supposed to come from a company like Apple. It does not track my walking steps accurately. My phone is brand new, no issues whatsoever, yet this app fails at the basic job it claims to do. Sleep tracking? Forget it. The data is either missing, false, or so off it might as well be a random number generator.

The worst part? Everything has to be added manually. Isn’t this supposed to be a “smart” health app? There’s no simple way to start a walk, track a workout, or monitor my activity in real time. And good luck finding any intuitive options, there are none. Zero user-friendly design, no responsiveness, and it feels like an unfinished product shoved onto your phone by default.

Apple constantly pushes overpriced products and drowns every app in paywalls and subscriptions, but when it comes to actually delivering value, they vanish. For a company that charges premium prices, it’s shameful how poorly this app performs. It’s clear they care more about squeezing money out of users than actually building functional, reliable tools.

Apple Health is a joke. Do better.

title: A nice app that has Promise, Could be improved.
body:
I stumbled across this app & I'm glad that I did! What I enjoy the most is the 'Mental Wellbeing' category, particularly the Mood Tracker! I really like logging how I'm feeling during parts of the day & also logging my overall mood for the day! It's so clever how I can drag the button on the bar left or right to indicate whether my current mood and/or my day is 'very unpleasant' to 'neutral' to 'very pleasant'. And I also like how it's also matched with varying shapes as well as different hues of purples, blues, & greens! 😃 

One thing that is lacking throughout the app is the ability to EDIT entries that you've previously logged, in ALL the categories, not just in the Mood Tracker. For example, I'd like the ability to edit a previous log entry (if I want to add or change an emotion) in the Mood Tracker. And like someone else said in their review, I'd also like the ability to add my own personal emotions in the 'emotions list'. 

Overall, it's a neat & well-thought out app & it amazes me that it was included with my iPhone (didn't cost anything extra)! I really hope that Apple reads the reviews & then works on improving the app, as it has promise to become an app worthy of 5 ⭐️s!

title: Meh
body:
It’s ok. I can’t order the categories or hide them so it tries to shame me about how much I move around when it has no idea because I leave it on my desk all day.

Also, too many ads. This is a problem because while Apple claims to treat my privacy with the respect that law and human decency demand, but I don’t remotely believe they’re curating these apps which are not I’m any way HIPPA compliant. I’m fact, many, if not most, are from companies that make the criminals that used their “analytics” contracts to steal confidential medical information. So that’s a concern.

Another concern is the privacy practices Apple claims. Are they eavesdropping on my private medical information? They say they collect this data. Do they actually mean collect or do they mean the app has access to it? Like other apps it’s self reported and open to interpretation. Personally, I choose to opt out. Enough studies have shown data can’t be truly anonymized.

A lot of this data is just flat out wrong. It doesn’t have any context I don’t give it but makes wild assumptions about things like how I walk based on my time standing in line. I can’t delete some of this stuff. It’s very frustrating and insulting.

I did give them back a star though for not being G—gel or Micr-S-ft, but it does feel like that toxic corporate culture that never wants to admit mistakes, even if there’s no liability or it’s the only way to fix them.

body: This app has a nice layout and spread of health factors to track. It’s helping me keep track of a number of health things in one place, which is convenient. I am very frustrated by the data entry itself. There are a lot of little automatic things that make life difficult such as: often something I enter about the end time of an activity changes the start time so I have to go enter it again. If I miss the change, the data ends up incorrect. Sometimes the data is incorrect in a way that impacts other data in the app. When I try to edit the data, the only thing to do is delete the whole entry. So, today, because I entered sleep at 10am instead of 10pm accidentally, it ended up linked to my previous days’ sleep. I can’t fix it without reentering yesterday and today. Frustrating. Being able to edit just a single part of the data is really key. Beyond that, to really love the app, I’d need it to be more customizable. When I log moods and feelings, the feelings I want are rarely there. I’d like to be able to add a customized type of exercise I do all the time. I’d like to be able to specify whether nutrients are food or supplements. It would be icing on the cake if I could just say which foods I’d eaten and have it track nutrients for me. It’s an app that I now use daily, and also wish I could be in charge of improving daily.

title: Ridiculous
body:
The Apple Health app is a powerful hub for tracking your wellness, but its full potential isn’t obvious out of the box. While most people assume it only becomes useful with an Apple Watch, the truth is your iPhone alone—combined with the right third-party apps—can measure and log a wide range of health data.

What Your iPhone Can Already Track

iPhones come equipped with advanced sensors like:
	•	Accelerometer & Gyroscope – Track movement, orientation, and steps.
	•	Barometer – Detects elevation changes and stair climbs.
	•	Magnetometer – Measures magnetic fields.
	•	Microphone – Can detect sound levels in your environment.
	•	GPS – Tracks distance, speed, and location-based activity.

The Apple Health app automatically logs steps, distance walked, flights climbed, and other basics using these sensors. But when paired with third-party sensor apps, things get way more interesting.

Boosting Health Data with Sensor Apps

Apps like SensorLog, Physics Toolbox Sensor Suite, and Sensor Kinetics can tap into over 100 different sensor inputs from your iPhone. These include:
	•	Environmental noise (decibel levels)
	•	Magnetic field data
	•	Acceleration spikes (which can suggest physical activity or respiration patterns)
	•	Orientation, gravity, and linear movement
	•	Altitude and barometric pressure changes

While Apple doesn’t let these apps write all data types directly into the Health app, some can export logs that can be manually imported or synced using bridge apps or shortcuts. This opens the door to creative uses—like using elevation and acceleration changes to infer breathing patterns or movement habits.

What Could Be Better

Apple doesn’t surface all of the available sensor data in Health natively, and tighter integration with sensor apps would make this platform truly next-level. You shouldn’t have to jump through hoops to track things your iPhone already knows.

I wish they would do this instead of rely on Apple watches. I mean pulse yeah but still.

title: Great App but Needs More Options for Logging Health Data
body: I started using this app about a month ago. So far it has accurately tracked my sleep, medications and other data. It linked to my health records and accurately links to my fitness app. I love that my information has been easy to input and that it’s all kept in one place. I see a cardiologist, a gastroenterologist, a primary physician, and sometimes the hospital. It’s very helpful to be able to accurately log details and data to share at my appointments across various providers. The only feature I would love to see is more detailed tracking. I have to keep a food journal and unfortunately a bathroom log. This is true for many people with GI issues and it would be awesome if there was a category or feature to be able to log this info within this app as well. Also, when I do have a time period where I’ve experienced a medical event that prevents me from reaching my fitness goals or that affects my daily habits it would be nice to be able to log that event so when I look back at my data I know why it was out of range for those days and I can accurately communicate to my various providers the dates, times, and details of those events without having to keep those notes in a separate form. I can only relate to the medical issues I have but I am sure there are other conditions out there that could benefit from more options of what to track and how to log medical procedures and events that affect our daily habits and routines. Overall this app has been very helpful and has great potential, I would recommend.

title: Medication Tracking works well

It has some minor quirks, but the important thing is that it’s trustworthy.  I finally feel I have something I can trust.  Thanks Apple.  

My main outstanding complaint is that it seems to be a little weird if I take a medication so late that it ends up being after midnight, so not taken until the following day. title: Tons of Room For Improvement
body:
While I love all the features this app has to offer, I can’t trust that the data is correct. 

Here are just a couple of the more notable issues: 

1) I’ve linked this app to my InBody app and confirmed that it is linked to this app as a data source, however, the app shows I weigh 28 pounds more than my last weigh in with the data showing as collected yesterday. When I input the proper number, it does not update. 

2) The VO2 Max scale is way off though I didn’t expect much from this feature as it does not have an “average” range. It goes straight from below average to above average with no chart for reference. So, if you were considering using this app to track your running progress, you’d be led astray. Not sure how this made it past testing and into prod.

Because these 2 features are so wrong, I have no confidence that the data provided from the other features is correct. Thus, the app is a waste.

title: Great data! But…
body:
The app has great features. For instance, I love having the lab records and the specialist records in the same  place. Also, the information on drug interaction is very valuable. But probably the best of all is that it integrates in one place the data collected by other apps and devices.

However, the app makes very simple mistakes. For example, the reason I started using it was as medicine reminder. I entered the first two daily medicines and scheduled them to be taken at 11 PM. The first night, I forgot to take them so I took them at 7:00 AM. The problem is that you can change the time (not intuitive at all, but finally I tap on the time and moved the time wheel up), but you cannot change the date. Result? I can’t find the log. This is the most important function when dealing with health and it did it wrong! The app has a lot of valuable features, but without medicine reminders I am not that willing to enter all my medicines there. 

New features suggested:

Viewers for X-ray, MRI, and other images. The could be stored in a special album (with sub-albums) in Photos. 
Vaccination records. Integrate with the doctor’s office and the pharmacies. Allow me to enter the information manually, if needed. It should be replaced by the automatically uploaded data when available. Make it easy to find. The first version does not need to have crazy COVID-like characteristics for identification or traveling. Make it just a list of taken vaccines as shown in the COVID card, but include any kind of vaccine. I want to see there my yellow fever vaccine along with the flu shot. 
Include dental information. It would be so useful!!!
The app is very disorganized. It is difficult to navigate and has unwanted information everywhere.
Why Favorites is not on top of everything? In Summary, it appears under all medical records section. 
Allow to add notes when I mark the medicine as taken. 
Make it easy to get the data not only from the UI, but also from Excel or my Python code.

title: Disappointed- sleep tracker and walking tracker
body:
My Samsung watch would catch my occasional naps during the day and add to my sleep totals. iWatch only tracks during the sleep window I create. Seems like such an expensive watch with so many touted features should be able to keep up with Samsung. 

When I walk (exercise of 5-8 miles most days) the watch often pauses recording. I have to constantly look at the watch face to see if it’s suddenly paused. Sometimes, I can feel a sight vibration but most times I don’t feel any notification. 
The watch should just behave appropriately when I am on the walk tracker. Very disappointing and rather unsafe to have to constantly divert my eyes and attention to the walk tracker. 

I use very few of the watch apps but cannot delete the unused apps. Obviously, they use battery. I often have to charge my iWatch twice during a 20-hour period. Presume Apple bloats the apps to collect fees from 3rd parties. 

Expensive digital purchase doesn’t deliver on what I need and what is promised.

title: Enhancing Period Tracking and Sync Capabilities
body:

title: Unit conversions
body:
The app won’t do unit conversions on imported data.  In my case, as a rower I measure my workout distances in meters using a variety of apps, Crew Nerd being one.  When Apple Health imports these data it doesn’t record any distance because it’s not in miles.  So my overall workout distances and anything calculated from that are absolutely meaningless.  As an aggregator of data it (Apple Health) interfaces with a wide variety of data sources but the results are not very useful.

It also fails to calculate VO2 fitness from anything except the Apple Watch workout app.  Walking, Running and Swimming are all used in that calculation but rowing isn’t.?!  I barely lift my HR off resting when I walk the dogs so Apple is convinced I’m very fit.  If it used my rowing workout HR’s it would be a different (but more meaningful) story!

OK app, but it’s fitness related sections need lots of work.

body:

My protection and sexual activity is solely based off of this app, and it has not failed me for the last 10 years. So long as I check in during the act or within a few hours of. 

HOWEVER: period symptoms need to be expanded.
 
What needs to be added:
Bloating
Diarrhea
Sensitive breasts
Muscle soreness 
Lack of patience 
Sleepiness
Emotional changes (with subdivisions of anger or sadness/sensitivity)

These are all factors that contribute to me knowing when I’m about to start my period. It is frustrating that when I go to the app, none of these are listed, but then I see my “cycle window” and realize I am about to start menstruating in the next 5 days or so. 

Should the app include these “symptoms” I would know my cycle is approaching much sooner.

body: My physician suggested that I get an Apple Watch to track a-fib occurrences and heart rate. Worst purchase ever. Sometimes something like steps will randomly synch between two of the devices (inconsistent as to which two), but not regularly. The guy at the Apple Store checked the settings on all three devices and said, well, you’ve got it set up correctly, and then he suggested that my cellular provider must be the problem. Eye roll. Worthless. Isn’t interoperability the whole point of committing to “the Apple brand?”

title: Not user friendly
body:
The health app is just a hot mess. Some apps log data in the health app, some only partially do it right, and no app logs all of its data to the health app correctly. Both cronometer and carb manager fail to log everything that is available in their own apps into Apple health, carb manager doesn’t update weight either. This is stuff that needs to be standardized BY Apple so it fits into this app. 

Medications that you must take multiple times a day fail to show up as a partially fulfilled circle of your day- taking one dose makes it look like you took everything you needed for that day. Dangerously misleading. 

The UI is B A D. What an absolute cluster. Open the app, first page is called summary, but it’s a mile and a half long page of a ton of useless info and ADVERTISEMENTS for other health apps. They shoehorn in links to articles in the summary and in the browse pages. If I wanted health articles I’d open safari and search. This app should be a data oriented app. 

Apple has the ability to take this app and turn it into an all-in-one health nutrition medication and sleep health app. Instead it’s a virtual dumping ground for third party apps. Apple, you can do better. We all want you to do better.

title: There could be so much more…
body: Before I start with the ways to improve I want to first applaud all of the pluses that heath and fitness apps offer. It’s a wonderful motivator to see just in time data and progress prompts and motivators such as badges. I love sharing my progress with friends and motivating each other. I adore the smiles we share through that. As an asthmatic, I rely on the blood oxygen readings that my watches record and use it to see my data regularly. I use my medication reminders religiously. (I wish it were easier to edit your time schedule for each.) Now…what I wish would be possible. We start each day on a calendar day. I wish the first question of the day with the health app was …how are you doing today. Healthy—great…let’s go. Not feeling so great….ok…here are some suggestions. Or Sicker than a dog with the flu, a cold, an asthma related allergy attack…that then adjusts the notifications you receive. I cannot tell you how discouraging it was to recently to be sicker than a dog in bed not able to move to have health/activity tell me to stand and exercise. Instead, it should be reminding me to drink, eat what I can, take the meds I need (have me list then as mine as interventions—of course I’d never expect the app to tell me. Let me build it. Why? This lets me further track my own data. Which brings me to the next I wish. I wish it were easier to analyze/export my data. Let me dump it in a spreadsheet and manipulate. Or better yet…give me the data I’ve collected in reports and rewards to help me grow further and align my goals. That’s a start of my brain dump. Would love to work further on how to make it better as someone who wants to be better every day and stick with apple products and not have another app.

I’d say that there is a fair amount of lag between the data on watch vs what’s displayed on the phone. I for one would love to see a tweak to the app to patch up the lag to make a much more premium feel which I believe the customers deserve based on the cost of these products. 

There is also a feature I believe would also heighten the premium feel that some other competitors may offer. The first that comes to mind is during a walk or run workout please provide step tracker as well. This will help many millions of avid tracking enthusiasts enjoy such features all the more and would probably drives sales in the short and long term.

I hope this is something that is strongly considered. Either way - thank you for your time. 

Best,
FNF

author: Chubbyslatte

title: Excellent for those who take Rx.
body:
I used the “Reminder” app to make sure I take my medications throughout the day. The “Health” app reminds me to take my pills. It also informs me of any drug interactions. Dizzy spells, almost passing out! App showed the offending drugs (severe interaction) giving me the opportunity to discuss with my health professionals. 
As of this review I have one request. Please add the ability to print. Whenever I visit my doctors, I take a list (Numbers) of current drugs. Printing would make it easier for me. Instead of two apps I would only need “Health” to record my medications. The medical staff is always grateful for the current list. 
Thank you!
author: Pooh Ba

title: Not for stair climbers.
body:
I don’t know why but this app is incapable of accurately keeping track of the flights you climb if you climb more than two flights in one day.
Every Wednesday and every Sunday I climb seven flights of stairs to get to church which is located on the seventh floor of a commercial building with twelve foot ceilings and at least three feet between floors.
Some days it only credits me with on floor. Sometimes two. The most it has recognized is four. 
Every time it’s seven up and seven down.
The map app I use is sensitive to a few inches of elevation. Why can’t this one accurately calculate seven floors?

title: Fails to meet expectations
body: Other apps such as Tidy Health are much better. Apple includes a new tool in Health app that lets you create a list of your current medications. It looks impressive but falls short in several critical areas. Each pill has an icon that is artificially created and does not picture the actual medication. Notifications are too numerous and generic to be practical and if those I share with forget to tap their Taken buttons I get nervous unnecessarily. The educational content is superficial and I wonder how reliable all those interaction alerts are? What this app lacks is even more disappointing - no place to put discontinued meds, no separate list for vitamins and supplements or OTC meds, no expiration reminders, no way to post photos of prescriptions or labels, no pharmacy info, not even Rx number. Apple could have done better. Again Health app fails to meet expectations.

author: Yiana28

title: Not great for pregnant people
body:
I’ve used this app for years along with my Apple Watch. I’ve found the information that it provides helpful in the past. 

Then I got pregnant. While the app lets you log your pregnancy in the cycle tracker, there’s no way to let other parts of the health app know that you’re pregnant. 

This is especially annoying when you’re using features like the heart rate tracker because it’s constantly telling you that it’s concerned about the rise in your resting heart rate. This leads to a first time mom like me worrying that my heart rate is too high, just to find out that a slightly higher heart rate is normal in pregnancy.

I’ve had plenty of other moments like this that lead to panic, followed by annoyance when I find there’s nothing to worry about. This can be easily fixed if the developers added new perimeters to their features that could be activated when pregnancy is logged. For now, I guess I’ll just have to find another way to track my walks.

The function is from Apple, but when I talked to Apple Health App Customer support, they said the issue came from the one who create the document, he didn’t want to see what is actually happening, just assume and hang up the app. It’s APPLE, only APPLE can do that with their customer, no review function to the customer support also.
author: Bill Pain

title: It doesn’t track ADHD meds as medications that affect heart rate, otherwise love all the data
body:
There’s an option to add “medications that affect heart rate” in the health app but it only allows for traditional heart meds and not other non-heart meds that also affect the heart. My ADHD meds raise my BP and my heart rate and it’s important to keep track of that because I’m also fairly athletic, so when I don’t take my meds my resting heart rate is very low, like in the 40’s, but when I take my meds my resting heart rate is in the mid 50’s to upper 60’s. It makes a big difference when calculating my max HR for my workouts. My zones are really inaccurate right now because of it. 

I just did a 2 hour workout with 75% in Zone 4 and 25% in Zone 5 according to my watch. It did not feel that hard! I wish that data was more accurate.

author: grubbycolonel

title: Laughably Dreadful
body:
What is this? Honestly? CLUNKY. Full of fluff. I used a FitBit for 6 years. I got an apple watch thinking it would be an amazing step up. But the health and fitness apps are SUBPAR. The stats are all over the place. Nothing is streamlined. Information that the Fitbit offers simple doesn’t exist…. I could never understand why my friends never wore their watches to bed. Now i get it. Because the sleep tracker on the apple health app is a MESS and doesn’t auto track. You have to get another app for that. 

Before you know it you’ll have to get and pay for a plethora of apps that a Fitbit watch offers for FREE! You’ll never know how many total calories you've burned with this. You'll never know your natural sleep patterns w this app. The 02 reader just doesn't exist now. 

You’ll need to click 5-10 different things to get to something that should only need 1-2 navigations MAX. 

I could go on and on. And I've only had this for One week.

Disappointed. Yes.
Surprisingly i cant imagine recommending and Apple Watch to anyone who is a health or fitness enthusiast.

Pardon me now as i switch back to my Fitbit for proper sleep tracking tonight.

title: Many shortcomings
body:
I’m not sure what database this uses for the meds, but it’s missing a lot. When I try to create compound meds, I can’t put the milligrams of the components in. Or for multivitamins, which are mostly missing, if I have to me the one to create it, I should be able to put the milligrams of each of the components. 

Vitamins and multivitamins should be listed by brand I think. Each company has slightly different formulae for multivitamins for example. This is woefully missing. 

Also for med schedule, not all meds are permanent. Many, like antibiotics, are only for a week or two, but we cannot put in end dates. After end date, the prescription should automatically go to the archives. It maybe should ask how missed doses should be treated, if it adds a day to the duration or not.

title: Re-order Favorites; more Mood options; log Migraines
body:
Please put a little effort into it! Someone designed this over a weekend 10 years ago and it was never improved. 

1. There’s no way to add Notes to an entry.

2. There’s no way to log a Migraine, which is different than an ordinary headache. I’m sure there are other health conditions that people would like to log that aren’t in the app, so let us customize our own. 

3. Users need to be able to drag and customize the order of Favorites. Shouldn’t be a big effort for the app developers. 

4. Also, the State of Mind logs need more options of factors that affect one’s mood. “What’s having the biggest impact…”? “Health” is too a broad category. How about Insomnia, Back pain, Financial, Menstrual cramps, dehydration, hangover… just add some factors or link other Health data to the mood. 

Ideally, it would be great to link the Apple Weather app to the Health app.
author: ecbpdx

title: Fitness Data obsessed traveler not happy
body: Apple needs to fix a bug that happens primarily when a user travels West through multiple time zones. I’ll wake up early in Europe and workout and get well over 15000 steps before boarding my flight and heading back to the West coast of the United States. The health app will correctly log that activity. Then as I travel west the steps for the days will start to decline and usually show less than 10k steps by the time I land. The formula then will add my steps to the previous days steps and make it appear as if I haven’t done activity on the date of arrival in the US.

title: Glitch?
body:
When I first synthesized this app with my Fitbit, this app started logging and projecting — through midnight and including while I was asleep — hourly “- steps.”

Today I woke up to see that this app has logged and projected “+ steps” — over 100 per hour every hour — from midnight (including while I was asleep) through midnight.

author: Samuraiferret

title: Terrible analytics & data accessibility
body: The app layout and functionality is AWFUL. It’s difficult to navigate and find what you’re looking for. Graphs and charts don’t have axes. And what’s wrong with line charts for time series data??? There’s no way to customize charts. It’s extremely difficult to find, download and analyze your data. Spent an hour on google searching how best to do this. Only way is to download ALL metrics combined in an XML file that requires a lot of manual manipulation to structure it into a usable format. HealthKit seems promising but only if you want to create an app for anyone to download from Apple Store. What about my own personal app (eg. a Power BI report) with real time health data (and only because this Health app is so awful!)? I’m really reluctant to download third party apps due to lax data privacy and security for most apps. PLEASE Apple, allow us to take control of and own our data in a more accessible and secure way!! If this option is already available via HealthKit, then this needs to be more clearly communicated.

title: Cycle Deviations - Missing the Point!
body:

I track my cycles with this app and my doctor has confirmed that I’m in perimenopause. I keep getting Cycle Deviation notices, and there was a list of possible conditions - except Perimenopause/Menopause!  

It is certainly true that skipped periods without pregnancy can be a cause for alarm. But it’s also expected. I would like to continue tracking without this app assuming that I don’t know what’s happening with my body. Yes, I’ll say it again - it’s menopause!

Now leave me alone, here comes another hot flash!

As far as improvements I would love to see more in depth sleep tracking and metrics such as those featured in the Autosleep app. The biggest update I would like to see is stress tracking. All the key essentials are in place with the Apple Watch for this to be a reality. Garmin is ahead of Apple in this category as even their $250 Venu Sq 2 tracker features body battery and stress tracking. As someone who battles anxiety and stress this would be a great feature to identify situations that are having the biggest effect on my anxiety and stress levels. Overall I’m happy with Apple Health but there’s lots of room for new features and improvements.  Another feature that is really needed in my opinion is the ability to track naps using sleep focus. title: User needs ability to add medical records
body:
The app is a very good start, but it needs some additional options. 

I turned off all the fitness stuff that is a waste of time to me and the doctors. I just use the daily vitals gathered from BP, Heart, and O2 device apps. 

The main reason I have for using this app is to consolidate medical records and heath data into a single, shareable, source, so that I can provide that data quickly and accurately to all providers of my health care that need to know.
 
When you see a provider. Time is very limited. Trying to remember, convey, and for them to correctly record, that important past history is an area where most mistakes occur. This mis-information, or the lack of important information, waste valuable time and money when those things really matter the most.
 
Some heath providers don’t use Apple Health and this void in critical information creates gaps in the overall knowledge needed to make accurate and meaningful diagnoses of the true root cause of a medical condition.

Please provide users with the ability to add documentation and complete medical data.

I can understand keeping user inputs separate from data gathered from the providers, but at least make it an available option. This would take this app to a whole new level of efficiency and usability.

author: Aminitee

title: Helpful but lacking
body:
I love that I can keep all my health info in one place, and synching with other apps is super helpful. However, I have several health issues I need to track, but there’s no way to add custom metrics. I use a habit tracking app for them, but I would rather use the health app so I can see the trends and more easily identify the relationship between different health metrics, and it’s easier to only have to check one app when I’m reviewing things with my doc. The sleep feature is also really annoying. It wants me to set a sleep schedule, but that means it thinks I’m sleeping when I’m not. So whenever I am ready for bed, I reset the schedule for the night. If I sleep past the schedule, I get woken up with alerts and notifications, so I have to set my sleep wake time for later than I think I’ll need, in case I sleep in (on days I don’t work), but when I do wake up, apparently I can’t turn off sleep focus because then it thinks I didn’t sleep at all. I’ve noticed a connection between my deep sleep minutes and my energy levels, so I just started a new medication to help me sleep better. Turned off sleep mode when I woke up this morning which apparently told the health app I didn’t sleep at all, so I have no data from last night to include in my tracking, to see how well the med is working. I would really like to just tell it when I’m going to bed and when I’ve woken up for the day and let it track sleeping habits during that time. I really like the new medication tracking feature. I have adhd so I often forget if I’ve taken something or how long it’s been since I last took something and I want to take the next dose instead of being reminded by the return of pain. It doesn’t allow you to change dosage, though. Dosage amount is part of the pill name/identity, so if you increase/decrease dosage, you have to archive one pill and create a new one. I’d rather see the changes in the chart that shows your history and frequency with that medication- can help identify that another health metric changed when a medication dosage changed.

So, the app is helpful but could definitely be more helpful with a few improvements!

author: DodgeGirl06

title: Great Concept that needs tweaks
body:
Overall I am very happy to have this app. I do think there is something rather tedious in how any manual data is entered or read. I have multiple health issues & had to take early retirement due to disability. I am on a very fixed income. So paying for apps, particularly for multiple health apps is onerous. For something I have a very legitimate need for I find all this frustrating. I do believe the designers are worthy of their remuneration, yet something feels very out of balance here. I had the opportunity to obtain an Apple phone. But I do wonder if I should have stuck w something cheaper as Apple app fees add up rapidly. 
       Would it be workable economically speaking to have a means of applying for some sort of basic fee for related health apps? Something Income based? Or are you only a company for those who can afford you? Nutrition apps, fitness apps, wellness routine apps. I have used all of these. Probably I could use means of logging mental health symptoms as well. I mention wellness routine apps as I need reminders to do simple things like brushing my teeth, & washing up. 
       The shortcut to Log Water quit working & I have not been able to figure out how to get it working again. I have to enter that data manually, as well as memorize or calculate the ounce-to-milliliter conversion. That becomes rather tedious. 
         I am female & can see the usefulness of tracking period cycles. However, someone has completely overlooked the concept of menopause. Particularly how much of life women can be post-menopausal. Granted at least I cannot turn this on. But I get tired of your constant articles or advice to record my cycle. Do you have women working on this? Anyone old enough to think of the concept. Please let me mark that I am post-menopausal or have had a uterus removed, anything that lets the app know I do not need this feature at all. Seriously. Great if ai still needed it, wish it had been available. Now I wish I could turn off this assumption I have used for this. I feel like this is another cog oddly enough in a male-dominated thought process. I guess it could be age-related as well. Just limited thinking typical of business stereotyping in some way. That is annoying.

title: Medication management is too clunky
body:
The two use cases I need these app to support are: 1) remind my husband to take his meds at specific times, and 2) provide a quick list of current meds and dosages that I can read off or share with a health provider. 

The app does an ok job on notifications. I wish however it would simply provide a list and not display the notes associated with each Med. I need my husband to be able to see a list that fits on the screen so it’s easy to compare the list to his bottles. 

The app does a poor job of sharing a complete list of meds. The EXPORT PDF list only displays the medication name and the pill unit. It does not display dosage (eg take 1mg 3 times per day). In order to communicate dosage, you have to go back into the schedule and scroll through the dang list. 

It’s too clunky. We have gone back to using a shared Note and a Clock alarm.

title: Good app.
body:
I really love this app. I love how Apple is starting to get into the healthcare aspect of smart Devices. However, I really wish Apple could release a few more products. 

I would love to see an apple smart Wi-Fi and Bluetooth body weight scale. An apple smart Wi-Fi and Bluetooth glucose monitor for diabetes and an Apple Bluetooth and Wi-Fi blood pressure monitor. I really trust apple with this data. 

I know it might sound crazy to say that as I am generally a privacy focused user. But health is too much to ignore and the apple smart watch along with third party tools and the apple health app have helped my Doctor and I go into remission for my Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease. We were able to pinpoint some trends that needed to be worked on.

I am tired of managing the manual inputs from these other third party devices. If apple created them. I would so buy them. It would make my life a bit more easier. There is a market for this. I just hope Apple realizes this and spins up a healthy living department internally to create these devices.

title: Cycle tracking is a gaslight
body: Two years… two years and EVERY MONTH it says I will have a five week period and bleed for two weeks despite having a very regular (with a few exceptions) 4 week cycle with 5 day bleed and plugging in the data. Other things work great. I don’t know who these women are getting accurate predictions bc two years and it’s ALWAYS WRONG… by usually a week or more. It’s beyond useless it’s actually counterproductive. It’s like it’s trying to gaslight me that I’m perimenopause despite having no symptoms. Y’all need to check your algos, they drunk. Other apps do way better. Srsly. Is it a tracking app for us or an anti Natalist algo tricking women into despair? I mostly kid. But I’ve never experienced such a terrible cycle tracker. I would literally do better with no app at all. I do, in fact.
author: Dr. Ake

title: Great Logging, But Could Be Better
body:
I like the app since I can log a variety of my health data, but I have a few concerns and recommendations regarding the limits of this application.

My concerns are mainly on data I CAN’T add to Apple Health. The notifications are ok, but I mainly mean:
Move Minutes, Exercise Minutes, Stand Hours, Stand Minutes, and Walking Heart Rate.

My recommendations are mainly for the workouts. There can be additional data to pair with workouts. In addition to the Active Energy and Distance, it can include:
Indoor Workout, Time in Seconds, Resting Energy, and Manual Pacing Data.
An alternate solution to this would be to link the corresponding data to workouts when written, rather than vise versus only.

If these features can be included, then the flexibility of Apple Health can increase and provide possible satisfaction to others. I hope that’s the case someday.

title: What’s wrong with this app?
body:
I walked over 10 miles yesterday the app says I walked 668 steps despite the activity app logging my miles. It says that I only stood for 2 hours, despite being on my feet all day at work! It says that I only burnt 41 calories and worked out for 6 minutes, the activity app disagrees! Closed all my rings. Please fix this! Ok so I have 2 phones, both have the same Apple ID one watch paired… Lately the health app isn’t showing my stats from the watch at all. The phones barely update all month! I’d like to add that I also purchased a Fitbit and paired to one of the phones, nothing shows up. And it’s not syncing any of my health information from the app (I.e. it will not update my cycle at all despite the health app having an accurate log of it). Please at least fix the issue where neither phone now sees data from my watch.

So, I’ve been allowed to have my phone with me at work. Now I wear a watch and carry my phone in my hip pocket at all times. There is a huge difference between the activity app in my watch and the health app on my phone! How can I lose miles upon miles every single day? I was under the impression the phone must be at waist level or below… My hip pocket! So the phone somehow misses an average of 5 miles a day.

I’ve come to the conclusion that my heart rate has to be up for either to really log exercise. Some days it will say I’ve climbed over 18 flights of stairs, when I have just gone down one, other days it will say one flight when I have gone over 20!

title: Seriously flawed
body:
I use this app only because it came with a free blood pressure monitor provided by my insurerer. It records my pressure and sync with Apple Health for that it gets a star. 

But it’s so frustrating to use. I would like to skip it altogether and just put the measures directly into Apple health and view there. 

Mainly it’s the recurring annoyances over and over. It asks me to enable notifications about 3 times a week with daily use. It also asks me to enter meds but only allows daily meds so I can’t enter them yet keep getting reminders to enable meds. And it keeps prompting me to sync medical records even though my doctor isn’t supported. 

So it’s a constant negative experience every time I use the app of “oh neat, there’s my blood pressure…dammit it’s popping up something stupid again when I’m trying to view results.”

Also it detects abnormal heart rates but records nothing about them so it’s hard to talk with my doctor. My doctor listens to my heart and it seems normal. Normal ECG. They could refer me to an expensive cardiologist, but I don’t have enough info from the app to act. And my Apple Watch reports no abnormal rate. 

I previously used a Withings blood pressure cuff and it was so much easier and just recorded pressure.

title: Period tracker doesn’t follow traditional medical nomenclature
body: Doctor here - the period tracking app counts the days in a non traditional and imo useless fashion. If you are on day 14 of your cycle, there is no way to see that info. The app (or likely the man behind the app) thinks it’s useful to tell you how many days since your period ended. This way of marking the days is not useful to women. We need to know how many days since menstruation STARTED. Not how many days since it ended. As I rack my brain to figure out why Apple has seemingly no education on why this is the medically accepted and most useful way to track which day you are on, I keep coming to the same suspicion: This feature is geared toward men who need to know how many days since their partners stopped bleeding. No woman needs to know how many days have passed since the last drop of blood. We need ti know how many days have passed since the first day that it started. Please consult with a woman or obgyn to confirm this info. Love that I can see my wrist temperature though. That really helps. Also, there’s no way to track libido! This is an essential sign to track.  These things just have the slight aroma of misogyny. Obviously every man knows that women have no libido to track(sarcasm), and the only essential thing to know is how long has it been since the bleeding stopped in case they want to give it an extra day for things to freshen up prior to sex. It’s almost comical imagining the boardroom of men coming up with what they think is important in a period tracking app. Please make an update to align with standard nomenclature.

title: This is an app I really want to like
body:
I really have a kind of love/hate relationship with this app. I really like being able to track things like my weight, steps, exercise, body temperature, and even my exposure to noise. That’s probably the most frustrating part of this app is environmental noise exposure. There is nowhere to indicate on the app that I am wearing hearing protection when I run machinery. I do this on a regular basis for my job so of course I use hearing protection on a regular basis. but there’s nowhere to indicate that on the app. Know if the app went off and notified me that the environment was too loud, and I wasn’t wearing hearing protection, and it reminded me to wear hearing protection, that would be a whole different ball game. I appreciate being able to be notified when my environment is too loud, but, it should allow me to wear hearing protection, and indicate that on that part of the app.

I really think instead of only medication that part of the app should allow us to do things that are healthy for our body. Like, for example taking time each day to water my plants isn’t a medication but it’s healthy for me to do it. That should be allowed to be added in on the app so I don’t forget.

Also in the medication section, it would be nice if I could fill in my own amounts. So instead of having to put milliliters, I should be allowed to put ounces if I need to. It should also allow me to add in vitamins and other things that I have to take for my health as well. Not everything I do for my body is a pharmaceutical drug. In fact, I only take one pharmaceutical drug and it’s temporary. there are quite a few things I take that are all natural for my health, and there is no way I can indicate that on the medication section, or at least not the right amount or anything. I guess what I’m asking for is that it be more flexible instead of so rigid.

And as always, I am visually impaired. I really would appreciate it. If this app would work better with voiceover. Right now, I have it in large so I can see it, and it’s not like I spend all day, staring at the app, but it would be great if it function better with voiceover. developers only need to download a certain program off of the Internet for free to make their apps work with accessibility features on both computers and cell phones.

title: Apple Doesn't Care Anymore. Premium Price. Dime Store Ideas.
body:
Apple used to innovate and lead. Now they sit back, ignore everyone that is begging for them to be industry innovators, and then (if we the consumers are lucky) just copy what the competition has been doing for several years.
My new apple watch is the nail in the coffin. In done with my watch, my macbook, my ipads, my iphone.  I'm switching to Android/Linux EVERYTHING.

Why do I say all this? Because Apple health offers a horrible user interface both in the app and on the watch. Trying to end a workout just marks a lap/set. Have no clue how to stop the workout. The app has three pages; summary, sharing, browse. That's not comprehensive enough. There is way too much in each of those tabs.

What REALLY makes me mad is compared to the Garmin fitness tracker I got at a yard-sale, the Apple watch environment offers almost no metrics, workout analysis, interactive data. Pace is displayed as ##'##". What on god's green earth does that mean?! Pace should calculate your MPH. If you track walk lasting 20 minutes, can the watch not be able to cross multiply and divide in order to calculate your pace in "##.##mi/hour" it should not be displayed in any other format or ratio. It should be labeled "mi/hour".

Health wants me to volunteer information like medications, Medical ID, ICE, and incessantly tells me I'm listening to my audio too loudly. I'm an American. I don't care. I have early childhood hearing loss. Stop mothering us. I'm not a minor. You shouldn't be allowed to do this.

My biggest gripe is you don't provide a comprehensive and modestly interactive workout summary like Garmin Connect. At least go use and look at their product and take their ideas to implement yourself. It's bad enough you don't come up with ideas that benefit the consumer anymore, Apple. You're more interested in collecting biometrics and analytics to sell off. You are. And you have no shame that you've put us last and data collection first.

Apple is on its way down if this is how it wants to continue running its business. People won't pay premium for sub-premium much longer. Eventually the majority will wake up and Apple will lose.

title: Skipped Medications
body: You can schedule your medications by time of day. It’s easy to log the medications you’ve taken as it automatically timestamps when you took them (if you remember to do so when you actually take them). There is an option to indicate that a specific medication was skipped but there is a flaw in the design. It timestamps the skipped using the current time when it should be using the scheduled time. For example: If my schedule includes taking a pain pill at 1:00 PM and I realize three hours later that I never took it, and don’t plan to take it, and flag it as skipped, the app records it as skipped at 4:00 PM even though I actually skipped it at 1:00 PM. I can edit the time to correct it to show 1:00 PM instead.  Other than  this minor annoyance, I think the app is pretty good.

title: Good start but needs improvement
body: Overall, the app is pretty good, but it could use some improvement to become excellent. My review at this time we'll focus on the sleep feature and sleep tracking of REM cycles with the Apple Watch. I was really excited to see this feature launch, and it's the reason why I bought the Apple Watch. While it is really cool, here are some improvements that I suggest: - Capture times that people sleep outside of scheduled sleep hours (e.g. naps, going to bed early, sleeping in late). - Capture multiple sleep periods per night when applicable (e.g. someone waking up in the middle of the night, staying awake for an extended period of time and going back to sleep). - If possible, it would be really cool to also have more live data accessible when sleeping (for connecting with Shortcuts or app developers). - Provide more integration of sleep data into Shortcuts.

title: Data helpful; two suggestions for improvement
body:
Overall, I really like this app. It’s great to see so much detail about my health in one place. It helps me make decisions about how best to adjust my lifestyle (nutrition, exercise, sleep) to improve my overall health.  

I do have two suggestions for additions to the app. I have experimented with the app quite a bit and searched the online forums, but have not found a way to do the following. If there already are ways to do what I describe below, please disregard these suggestions. 

1. Please add a way to view total calories burned for a day. I don’t hate math, but having to add active and resting calories every day is a chore. I do realize the total calories burned can be found in the Fitness app; however, I’d like to use Apple Health the way for which, I believe, it was designed — a one-stop shop. It would be very convenient. 

2. Please add the option to view a Summary page of health data for any day in the past. In its current form, only a Summary of today’s health data is viewable. I understand I can go into each category (active energy, steps, resting energy, etc.) and from there select the day, week, month, or year I’d like to view. But it would be so helpful to see this data on one page. 

Thank you!

title: iPad & Widgets
body:
The health app is a great tool for tracking overall health. I would love to see some additions, however. 

I have ADHD. A part of that is chronic forgetfulness. (Specifically object impermanence). A customizable health widget would let me see important information right on my Home Screen. The medication I’m on increases blood pressure, so I dutifully monitor mine. A widget would help remind me to take/record readings throughout the day, along with sharing trends in my BP. 

I understand the hesitance in displaying sensitive information on the Home Screen, but limiting the type of info available to non-sensitive stats would be enough. Heart rate, BP, Water intake, rings, weight, etc. An additional Face ID check could be implemented upon opening the app (if it’s not already an option). 

An iPad/Mac app would be very helpful, as I spread my workflow amongst multiple devices. I rarely use my phone during working hours. When I do, it’s typically only for communication. Having a Mac/iPad app/widget would remind me to check in and would assist in prioritizing my health.

title: Great for integrations, awful as an app
body: You can think of Apple Health as the consumer portal for HealthKit. It has the best integrations with every app (think Withings or Peloton or MyFitnessPal) of any aggregator. So Health is by far the best place to see all the data in one place. The problem is that it’s a terrible app. The good news is that fixing it shouldn’t be that hard. 1. The visualizations aren’t that good. Most of them are ugly, there are no trend lines (“trends” are super basic moving averages but being able to toggle them is great), and it doesn’t make use of other informative modalities like color changes. 2. Data isn’t linked together. For example when you go to workouts it should automatically pull up your heart rate during that workout. (And when you run it should be smart enough to pull up distance and running maps.) When you look at diet it should be easy to see a snapshot of your calories and macros. Your weight should also pull up other body composition. Steps should also let you see distance. Etc. This is just data coding and a little UI work. 3. Apple needs to bring in more data types. Period. Like more body composition measures, map tracking for running needs to work better, etc. 4. Health has very inflexible viewing periods. It’s week, month, year, etc, and that’s it. And when you zoom out a lot it shows averages and not real data. This doesn’t make much sense. You should be able to arbitrarily zoom in and out of any period and see your data automatically adjust. 5. The dashboard part isn’t that good. It’s like the Home app. Apple is fixing the Home app this year with a better Home Screen/dashboard. I hope they do the same with Health. It would be amazing to be able to pick a few priorities and get overviews. Like nutrition, my daily pills, some exercise stuff. The makings of the absolute best consumer health app is there. The integrations are the hard part and Apple has nailed it. Now they just need to make a better Home Screen and more intelligent visualizations. That’s not a heavy lift. Apple can do it!

title: Not even close to accurate
body:
As a former program manager for Nike Fuel Band I have been involved in fitness tracking intensely for about a decade. I have watched as within the last couple of years the algorithm has changed for the health app and unfortunately almost all downloadable apps use that toolkit. 

It started with me noticing at tge end of tge day I had hit a goal of x+20% but the next morning when I logged on it would suddenly show x-20% on the downloaded app I was using. As I investigated it became clear that the 3 I experimented with reset tge next day to not what they measured but what the health app measured. And it was always less than any of the three apps. 

Then today walking in Seattle I used GPS to track my route and several of tge apps. At around noon I was at according to the health app nearly 20,000 steps and went on another long walk when I was done it showed I had walked 18000 for the day. This was less than before tge walk!  In addition all of the GPS apps were showing in excess of 11 miles walked. And that would normally translate to ~25k steps. 

The app does not seem to have a trustworthy algorithm and it seems to arbitrarily subtract progress. Based on this I cannot recommend it or any app that relies on it which is essentially every app in the App Store if you actually want to track and rate your progress. If it is a casual “I wonder what I did today and accuracy is irrelevant then I would say it is better than nothing but barely.
